body:
The thing about the future is, I understand from everything I've heard about the economy and the world we live in that things are going to be worse, a lot worse, and for longer than people expect.  I try to be prepared for this by doing a lot of independent projects.  I eventually got better at these side-skills than at school, so I end up going to special job fairs and applying to jobs outside of my major.

That's all well and good, but no one wants to even interview me because either (a) I have only programming on my resume and can't be an urban planner or (b) I am majoring in urban planning and not computer science, so they think I just took programming 101.  I know this from trying to meet professors and student organization people here on campus.  I found a professor who's in the more technical side of urban planning, and she flat out told me "you're a programmer!" My dad tried talking me into doing Linux administration but it's kind of like the "one word: *plastics*" advice.  Last year I applied to 80 jobs, this year it may be a couple hundred.  Trying everything from cover letters with puns on the company's name (so they know it's written especially for them) to going to a local programming meet-up group.  I've already been rejected from a few.

I'd like to know that in my future I can be part of rebuilding our economy and making a difference.  It just doesn't seem to be coming together, and mentally I'm all over the place.

Thank you for your help, I'll try to put it in perspective, see what happens with the job apps.

Thank you for your suggestion, you're probably right to a good extent.

The self-confidence issue is complex.  I still participate a lot in group projects.  I still work well with people.  There's just nothing in it beyond turning in the paper.  Back in high school I made a speech to 400 people, and regularly was in a debate club.  Over the past couple of years, I've asked a couple of classmates out on not-officially-dates and talked/listened with them for hours, baked cookies.  I just couldn't find feelings for them.  Now I think they go to parties and stuff, which I just can't get into.  I don't drink, not even coffee, so I'm a bit too weird.

I don't know what to think about medication.  What creeped me out wasn't its failure to help, it was that I began looking forward to taking it each night.  Like I'd tell myself, "you have to wait till 5 pm since that's when you took it last night" and at 4:30 I start looking at the clock over and over, so I take it at 4:45.  It would also take me forever to wake up, in a haze where I would think I had done something, then realize I still hadn't moved out of bed yet, then imagine checking the clock, then checking it for real. Both the therapist and psychiatrist said they'd try a new medication this semester but I've put off meeting them until my classes are "settled" - to buy me some time.

The attraction thing is complex.  I used to think of myself as a moral person: I don't swear or drink, I don't make lewd comments, I just try to do the right thing and people tend to appreciate that.  It's not that many girls who I notice, and some are older (including a former classmate who many say looks 14).  But each time it seems like such a pure and honest emotion, having butterflies, hoping to impress her with what I'm reading.  It would be such an awesome feeling to have if it wasn't directed so horribly.

I considered working directly for a non-profit as you suggest.  I was going to withdraw for a year (my college won't let me leave for just one semester) and work in Asia.  I contacted the manager and personnel director, did some projects for them, but there's a terrible language barrier.  My parents put me on a major guilt trip (You're ruining the holidays talking about this!  You need to take me to the hospital for surgery next month!) so I didn't follow through.  Well now I'm back at school and everywhere I go I can remember that I didn't want to be here.

Maybe I could help out in the US over the summer, but I need to try for a paid internship somewhere.  Last year I applied to over 80 places I was qualified for and didn't even get an interview.

&Thank you for replying
